attractions.name: Mim Bour
attractions.aliases: Mim Rocky Mountains; Mim Buo; Mim Bour Mountains
attractions.description: A group of three rocky peaks rising to about 410 m just west of Mim; the tallest is traditionally regarded as the father of the other two. The site has been partly developed for tourism with a reception centre, pool and gardens on the summit of the female mountain.

attractions.name: Mim Lake
attractions.description: A small inland lake on the outskirts of Mim, expanded from the natural Anwomasu river, that is preserved as a tourist and leisure site. It holds endemic and near-endemic cichlid fish including Hemichromis frempongi.

attractions.name: Mim Airstrip
attractions.description: An airstrip serving the Mim area, located east of the Mim Bour mountains. It is one of the few aviation facilities in the Ahafo Region.

attractions.name: Anwomasu Dam
attractions.description: A dam near Ayum Forest Products in Mim, connected by a conduit to Mim Lake, that historically served industrial and domestic water purposes.

attractions.name: Asumura White-necked Rockfowl Conservation Area
attractions.aliases: White-necked Rockfowl Conservation; Asumura Rockfowl Site
attractions.description: A conservation site near Akrodie and Asumura that protects the rare white-necked rockfowl, a species prized by birdwatchers for its appearance and nesting habits.

attractions.name: Okomfo Anokye Tree
attractions.aliases: Okomfo Anokye Historic Tree; Sankore Sacred Tree
attractions.description: A historic tree at Sankore associated with the legendary priest Okomfo Anokye and regarded as a sacred and heritage site in the Ahafo Region.

attractions.name: Tano River
attractions.aliases: Tano River; River Tano; Tanoe River
attractions.description: A 400 km river that drains the Tano Basin and flows through the forest belt around Goaso; it is culturally important to the Bono and Ahafo peoples and supports rich biodiversity.

attractions.name: Ahafo Mine
attractions.aliases: Newmont Ahafo Mine; Ahafo Gold Mine
attractions.description: One of the largest open-pit gold mines in Ghana, located in the Kenyasi area and operated since 2007, with estimated reserves of around 17 million ounces of gold.

attractions.name: Adekyem Festival
attractions.description: An annual November festival celebrated by the people of Bechem that commemorates historical events from the town's founding and raises funds for local educational development.

attractions.name: Abetiase Festival
attractions.description: A bi-annual festival held at Goaso that celebrates local traditions and the town's historic role in relation to the Golden Stool.

Ahafo._note: Fewer than 20 notable, specifically named attractions could be verified for the Ahafo Region from Wikipedia and the Ghana Tourism Authority (Visit Ghana). Only the entries above were verified from the fetched sources.

attractions.name: Gbewaa Palace
attractions.aliases: Naa Gbewaa Palace; Yaa Naa Palace; Gbewaa palace
attractions.description: The royal palace at Yendi, traditional capital of the Kingdom of Dagbon, and the seat of the Yaa Naa, king of Ghana's oldest kingdom.

attractions.name: Naa Binbegu Baobab Tree
attractions.aliases: Naa Binbegu Boabab Tree; Yendi Baobab
attractions.description: A historic baobab tree at Yendi listed by the Northern Region as a notable natural and cultural landmark.

attractions.name: Deutsch Cemetery
attractions.aliases: German Cemetery Yendi; Deutsch Cemetery at Yendi
attractions.description: A colonial-era cemetery at Yendi associated with the period of German involvement in the region, listed among the Northern Region's heritage sites.

attractions.name: Saakpuli Slave Wells
attractions.description: Historic wells at Saakpuli linked to the trans-Saharan and domestic slave trade routes of northern Ghana.

attractions.name: Adibo Dalila War Zone
attractions.aliases: Adibo dalila war zones; Battle of Adibo Site
attractions.description: The site of the 1896 Battle of Adibo near the village of Adibo, where Dagomba forces resisted German colonial troops; it is preserved as a historic war zone.

attractions.name: Tamale Center for Culture and Arts
attractions.aliases: Tamale Cultural Centre; Tamale Centre for Culture and Arts
attractions.description: A cultural centre in Tamale showcasing the arts, crafts and traditions of the peoples of the Northern Region.

attractions.name: Savanna Centre for Contemporary Art
attractions.aliases: Savanna Centre; Savanna Contemporary Art Centre
attractions.description: A contemporary art centre in Tamale promoting modern visual art from northern Ghana.

attractions.name: Red Clay Studio
attractions.aliases: Red Clay Studios; Red Clay Art Studio
attractions.description: An artist studio and creative space in Tamale known for working with local red clay and contemporary art practice.

attractions.name: Nkrumah Volini
attractions.description: A historic site in Tamale associated with Kwame Nkrumah and the nationalist movement in northern Ghana.

attractions.name: Nuku Studio
attractions.description: An art studio in Tamale contributing to the city's contemporary visual arts scene.

attractions.name: Hamamat Shea Butter Village
attractions.aliases: Hamamat Shea Butter Village; Hamamat Village
attractions.description: A shea butter processing and visitor village near Tamale that showcases traditional shea butter production.

attractions.name: Diarre Napagaduungbanani
attractions.description: A traditional heritage site at Diare in the Northern Region recognised for its historical and cultural significance.

attractions.name: Buntaga Irrigation Dam
attractions.description: An irrigation dam in the Northern Region used for agricultural water supply and listed as a regional visitor site.

attractions.name: Sabali River (River Oti)
attractions.aliases: Sabali; River Oti at Sabali; Sabali River
attractions.description: A stretch of the River Oti at Sabali in the Northern Region, noted as a scenic riverine site.

attractions.name: Nawuni River (White Volta)
attractions.aliases: Nawuni River; White Volta at Nawuni
attractions.description: The White Volta River at Nawuni, an important waterway and scenic natural site in the Northern Region.

attractions.name: Tamale Central Mosque
attractions.description: The principal central mosque of Tamale, one of the city's best-known landmarks and a focal point of Islamic worship in northern Ghana.

attractions.name: Tamale Central Market
attractions.description: The main market of Tamale, a major trading hub for grains, livestock, yams and crafts from across the Northern Region.

attractions.name: Aliu Mahama Sports Stadium
attractions.aliases: Tamale Sports Stadium; Aliu Mahama Stadium
attractions.description: Tamale's principal stadium, formerly the Tamale Sports Stadium, which hosted matches during the 2008 African Cup of Nations.

attractions.name: Tamale International Airport
attractions.description: The airport serving Tamale, located about 11 km from the city centre and operating regular domestic flights to Accra and other regional capitals.

attractions.name: Tamale Teaching Hospital
attractions.description: Ghana's third-largest hospital and the main referral health facility for the Northern Region, also used for medical teaching and research.

attractions.name: Dakpema Palace
attractions.description: The palace of the Dakpema, the traditional chief of Tamale, whose influence shaped the city's establishment as an administrative centre.

attractions.name: Mole National Park
attractions.aliases: Mole National Park; Mole Game Reserve
attractions.description: Ghana's largest wildlife refuge, covering about 4,840 km2 of savanna and riparian habitat and home to over 93 mammal species including elephants, hippos and antelopes.

attractions.name: Larabanga Mosque
attractions.description: The oldest mosque in Ghana, built in 1421 in the Sudano-Sahelian style, and often called the Mecca of West Africa.

attractions.name: Larabanga Mystic Stone
attractions.aliases: Larabanga Mystery Stone; Mystic Stone of Larabanga
attractions.description: A sacred stone on the outskirts of Larabanga believed to return to its original position whenever it is moved; British road builders reportedly had to divert a road around it in the 1950s.

attractions.name: Larabanga Baobab (Ayuba's Grave)
attractions.aliases: Larabanga Baobab; Ayuba's Baobab; Baobab of Larabanga
attractions.description: A baobab beside the Larabanga Mosque that is reputed to mark the grave of Ayuba, the mosque's founder, and whose leaves are used locally for healing.

attractions.name: Bole Mosque
attractions.description: A Sudano-Sahelian adobe mosque in the centre of Bole, dated to around the 17th century, which collapsed in 2023 and was rebuilt with traditional materials in 2024.

attractions.name: Bui National Park
attractions.aliases: Bui National Park; Bui Game Reserve
attractions.description: A 1,821 km2 national park established in 1971 and bisected by the Black Volta, notable for its hippopotamus population and the endangered ursine colobus.

attractions.name: Bui Dam
attractions.aliases: Bui Hydroelectric Dam; Bui Hydropower Plant
attractions.description: A 400 MW hydroelectric dam on the Black Volta at the Bui Gorge, commissioned in 2013 and the second-largest hydroelectric plant in Ghana.

attractions.name: Bui Reservoir
attractions.description: The reservoir created by the Bui Dam, with a surface area of up to 440 km2 and a haven for hippos, cormorants and other wildlife.

attractions.name: Bui Gorge
attractions.description: The rocky gorge on the Black Volta where the Bui Dam is built, noted for its dramatic terrain and first surveyed by geologist Albert Ernest Kitson in 1925.

attractions.name: Salaga Slave Market
attractions.aliases: Salaga Slave Market; Salaga Old Slave Market
attractions.description: The site of the largest slave market in 18th- and 19th-century Ghana, from which captives were shipped to the coast; a young baobab now marks the former market area.

attractions.name: Salaga Slave Tree
attractions.aliases: Salaga Slave Tree; Slave Tree of Salaga
attractions.description: A historic tree at Salaga associated with the town's role in the trans-Saharan and Atlantic slave trades and preserved as a heritage landmark.

attractions.name: Wonkan Bawa (Slave Bathing Pond)
attractions.description: A pond at Salaga whose Hausa name means the bathing spot of slaves, recalling the town's history as a major slave market.

attractions.name: Jakpa Palace
attractions.description: The seat, official residence and meeting place of the Yagbonwura, overlord of the Gonja Kingdom, located at Damongo and built in Malian architectural style.

attractions.name: St Anne's Catholic Cathedral
attractions.aliases: St Anne's Cathedral Damongo; Saint Anne's Catholic Cathedral
attractions.description: The cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Damongo and one of the town's principal landmarks.

attractions.name: Gonja Kingdom Traditional Seat
attractions.description: Damongo has been the seat of the Gonja Kingdom since the Yagbonwura's court moved there from Nyange in 1944, making it a centre of Gonja heritage.

attractions.name: Old Buipe
attractions.description: A historic settlement on the Black Volta associated with early Gonja history and the site of archaeological excavations of old Buipe.

attractions.name: Daboya
attractions.description: An old Gonja town on the White Volta that was a seat of Gonja kingship and is known for its historic mosque and archaeological heritage.

attractions.name: Kpembe Traditional Area
attractions.description: A traditional town just 2 km from Salaga that serves as the capital of the Kpembe Traditional Area, whose chief is the overlord of Salaga.

attractions.name: Mole Safari Lodge
attractions.description: The accommodation and visitor complex at Mole National Park, described as West Africa's first luxury safari lodge and the base for park game drives and walking safaris.

attractions.name: Salaga Slave Wells
attractions.description: Historic wells at Salaga that supplied water to the town's slave market and caravans, listed among the Savannah Region's tourism sites.

attractions.name: Gambaga Escarpment
attractions.description: An impressive line of cliffs running roughly 100 km and forming the northern boundary of the North East Region, with panoramic views over the White Volta plains.

attractions.name: NaYiri Palace
attractions.description: The chief's palace at Nalerigu and the traditional seat of the overlord of Mamprugu, serving as a centre of cultural activity in the region.

attractions.name: NaJeringa Defence Wall
attractions.description: A historic wall built in the 1700s by a Mamprusi king to defend the capital at Nalerigu against raiders; its remains are preserved as a heritage site.

attractions.name: Zayaa Mosque-Shrine
attractions.aliases: Zayaa Mosque; Zayaa Shrine; Zayaa Mosque/Shrine
attractions.description: A distinctive mosque and shrine at Wulugu with an intriguing mystical and spiritual history, noted for its unusual architecture.

attractions.name: Ancient Koma Figurines
attractions.description: Clay statuettes left behind by settlers over 1,000 years ago, discovered in the Yikpabongo area and important to West African archaeology.

attractions.name: Buyuori Cave
attractions.description: A large natural cavern east of Yikpabongo that can be explored on foot and is one of the region's notable natural features.

attractions.name: Tusugu Cliff Dwellings
attractions.aliases: Tusugu Cliff Dwellings; Tusugu Cliff Settlement
attractions.description: Well-preserved remains of an ancient settlement built into the Gambaga Escarpment, discovered in 1961.

attractions.name: Gingana Mountain & Rock Art
attractions.description: A scenic point on the Gambaga Escarpment overlooking the White Volta, notable for its ancient rock carvings and paintings.

attractions.name: Kpatiritinga Rock Art & Granaries
attractions.description: A site along the Gambaga Escarpment with rock art and centuries-old adobe granaries, among the region's most impressive recent archaeological discoveries.

attractions.name: Tanfiok-Naamaa Rock Paintings
attractions.aliases: Tanfiok-Naamaa Rock Paintings; Jilik Rock Paintings
attractions.description: Prehistoric rock paintings of hunters and animals near Jilik that researchers believe may date back to the Stone Age.

attractions.name: White Volta River Rapids
attractions.aliases: White Volta Rapids; White Volta River Rapids
attractions.description: A stretch just north of Gambaga where the White Volta rushes through rocks, creating dramatic rapids along the base of the escarpment.

attractions.name: Gbintiri Market
attractions.description: Held every six days, this is the largest market in the North East Region, drawing traders and livestock from across the area.

attractions.name: The Doves' Caves (Nmana Feeri)
attractions.aliases: Doves' Caves; Nmana Feeri; Doves Caves Nalerigu
attractions.description: A group of rock outcrops a short hike from Nalerigu, popular for bouldering, exploring and views over the surrounding savanna.

attractions.name: Fire Festival (Bugum Chugu)
attractions.aliases: Bugum Chugu; Fire Festival; Bugum Festival
attractions.description: An exciting annual festival celebrated in most Mamprusi communities across the region in remembrance of an old legend, marked by night-time fire processions.

attractions.name: Damba Festival
attractions.description: A major annual festival of the Mamprusi and Dagomba peoples, celebrated at the NaYiri Palace in Nalerigu with drumming, dancing and traditional regalia.

attractions.name: Birimi Prehistoric Site
attractions.description: An archaeological site near Nalerigu associated with the Kintampo Complex civilisation and ancient pearl millet cultivation.

attractions.name: Mamprusi and Mossi Kings' Gravesites
attractions.description: Ancestral grave sites of ancient Mamprusi and Mossi kings at Gambaga, which was once the residence of Mamprusi kings.

attractions.name: Gambaga Witch Camp
attractions.aliases: Gambaga Witch Camp; Gambaga Witches Camp
attractions.description: A settlement at Gambaga where women accused of witchcraft have historically sought refuge; it featured in the 2011 documentary The Witches of Gambaga.

attractions.name: Red Volta River
attractions.description: One of the two Volta headstreams flowing through the North East Region, offering canoeing and riverside scenery alongside the White Volta.

attractions.name: Nakpanduri Escarpment
attractions.description: A dramatic section of the Gambaga Escarpment at Nakpanduri, known for its cliffs, caves and panoramic views across the North East Region.

attractions.name: White Volta River
attractions.description: The major river of the North East Region, which together with the Red Volta forms the Volta River and is popular for canoeing.
